Street Fighter. A fighting game franchise launched by Capcom in 1987, featuring hand-to-hand martial artists competing in tournaments across the globe. Pioneering competitive fighting mechanics and esports culture, the series defined the genre and spawned a multi-decade competitive community centered on frame-data precision and split-second decision-making. The franchise debuted in 1987 as an arcade game, but Street Fighter II in 1991 revolutionized the genre by introducing eight distinct fighters—Ryu, Ken, Guile, Blanka, E. Honda, Chun-Li, Zangief, and Dhalsim—each with unique move sets and fighting styles.

Command inputs like quarter-circle motions and half-circles unlock special moves. Ryu's Hadoken fireball and Zangief's Spinning Piledriver require dexterity and memory. Combos, which are linked sequences of moves, reward execution skill. The game became an arcade sensation. Tournament players pushed the meta-game forward, discovering infinite combos and frame-trap sequences. Arcades became social hubs and proving grounds. Street Fighter II Turbo and Super Street Fighter II added new fighters and balanced matchups with variation speeds. Street Fighter: Alpha in 1995 introduced the Grooves system, giving three fighting styles per character. Street Fighter III in 2000 introduced parries, which block into forward to automatically negate chip damage, with a fifteen-fighter roster. Street Fighter IV in 2008 revived the franchise with three-dimensional graphics and Focus Attacks, an armor-breaking counterattack mechanic.

The modern competitive scene centers on Street Fighter 6, released in 2023, which emphasizes accessibility with a modern control scheme while still supporting traditional arcade-stick play. Esports titles like CEO, Combo Breaker, and Evo draw thousands of players. The franchise expanded into film with a Street Fighter movie in 1994 and Street Fighter 6 in 2023, as well as manga, and spawned the broader "fighting game" genre. Capcom is the developer and publisher, making Street Fighter a cornerstone of their arcade legacy. Ryu stands as the wandering martial artist protagonist, searching for worthy opponents, while M. Bison, the Dictator of Shadaloo, serves as the overarching villain connecting the lore.
